title: Choose the new BugReceipt landing-page structure
question: All three keep the current Evidence Desk palette and typography. Choose the composition that should govern the full redesign, combine elements in your note, or re-roll.

options.label: Field Manual Sequence
options.lineage: technical field manuals and annotated review plates
options.thesis: The page unfolds as a numbered operating manual for turning one failure into reviewable evidence.
options.viewport: A compact navigation rail sits above one oversized annotated plate: the benefit statement owns the left margin, the live extension workflow fills the center, and four evidence callouts lock to its edges.
options.risk: Can feel instructional before persuasive unless the benefit remains the largest idea in the fold.

raised.raise: Every evidence state gets a fixed, scannable row instead of floating feature copy.
A dense coral status band collides with the quiet paper field to make the first viewport memorable.

options.label: Failure Trace Timeline
options.lineage: incident timelines and browser performance traces
options.thesis: One uninterrupted diagnostic trace carries the visitor from record to inspect, remove, and export.
options.viewport: A tall benefit statement anchors the left third while a horizontal trace crosses the fold, docking the animated extension preview to the active event and previewing the later privacy and export checkpoints.
options.risk: The trace must stay semantic and calm or it can become a decorative stepper.

options.label: Triage Desk
options.lineage: QA triage boards and incident review tables
options.thesis: The first viewport behaves like a live triage desk where the report, evidence, and next action are visible together.
options.viewport: The headline forms a narrow top band; beneath it, an asymmetric three-column desk shows the issue summary, the live extension preview, and a compact local-export receipt with the download action embedded in the workflow.
options.risk: Density can read like the application itself if the marketing hierarchy becomes too quiet.
